Oct 25 : Anthropic's Claude bypassed a paywall and accessed publicly available US state of Georgia voter data without human authorization, Axios reported on Sunday. "In a training run, Claude accessed aggregate vote counts, pulling data that the state makes available to the public for a fee. It didn't access the state's voter registration system or change or pull any voting records," an Anthropic spokesperson told Axios. Reuters could not immediately verify the report.

Source: Reuters

Oct 26 : NEXTDC CEO Craig Scroggie will give up his fiscal 2027 bonus opportunities, the Australian data centre operator said on Monday, after it slashed its revenue forecast and paused future developments last week. Here are some details: • The company said the board has withdrawn the resolution proposing an approval of grant of performance rights and restricted rights to the CEO under the fiscal 2027 long term incentive plan. • Current Chairman Douglas Flynn has reaffirmed his intention to retire from the board once a new chairman is in place, after a short handover period.

BARCELONA, Oct 25 : Real Madrid became the first side to beat Barcelona in LaLiga this season, defeating the league leaders 2-1 at Camp Nou with a brace from Kylian Mbappe. Mbappe's 11th goal in 10 LaLiga matches secured victory for Jose Mourinho in his return to El Clasico 13 years after his first spell at Real Madrid ended. Real halved the gap to league leaders Barcelona to three points. Both sides created a series of half-chances early on, but Real's forays forward came with far more resolve. Barca manager Hansi Flick's frustration on the touchline served as evidence that Mourinho's game plan was functioning better than his own.

In the 41st minute, Yan Diomande crossed from the left and Gerard Martin's soft clearance hit the onrushing Mbappe, bouncing off him and into the net. Barcelona had the chance to level before the break after a fortunate ricochet, but Lamine Yamal couldn't convert from close range. It was a set piece that undid Real in the 61st minute, with Pedri's reverse pass finding Raphinha in space in the box and the Brazilian finishing into the corner. Real's swift movement of the ball in their own half continued to expose the Barcelona backline in the early stages of the second half. However, following the goal, the visitors found it increasingly hard to escape Barcelona's pressing. Barcelona's attacks were now finishing with last-ditch blocks from the Real defence, even if Mourinho's side continued to carry a threat going forward. That defensive conviction was rewarded with three minutes remaining. A loose touch from Barcelona substitute Gabriel Jesus set Real on the counter-attack, and substitute Eduardo Camavinga had enough pace to get in behind the defence, before squaring the ball for Mbappe to tap into the empty net. Barcelona remain top of the standings with 27 points from 10 games, one ahead of Atletico Madrid in second place. Third-place Real Madrid are on 24 points. Earlier Athletic Club beat Getafe 4-0 and Real Sociedad won 2-1 against Levante. Real Betis remain fourth after drawing 0-0 with Celta Vigo.

Source: Reuters

AUSTIN, Texas, Oct 25 : Kimi Antonelli won the US Grand Prix for Mercedes on Sunday to stand on the brink of becoming Formula One's youngest ever champion in Mexico next weekend. The 20-year-old Italian did all he could to put the championship out of reach of his rivals in Texas but Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Mercedes teammate George Russell did just enough to delay the inevitable with fourth and eighth respectively. Antonelli now needs to score only two points - a ninth place - in Mexico City to be sure of the title. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc finished second, 13.078 seconds behind, in Sunday's race at Austin's Circuit of the Americas with Red Bull's Max Verstappen third and helped by a late virtual safety car that slowed a chasing Hamilton who finished one second down the road.

The dominant win from pole position on a one-stop strategy was Antonelli's ninth of the season and he now leads Russell  by 123 points, and Hamilton by 124 with a maximum 125 remaining to be won and that reducing to 100 after Mexico. "It was the result we needed and the whole team deserve it so much," said Antonelli. "I know we're very close. We try to finish on a high and hopefully we can clinch it very soon".  McLaren's reigning champion Lando Norris finished fifth with Red Bull's Isack Hadjar sixth, and ahead of McLaren's Oscar Piastri. Liam Lawson was ninth for Racing Bulls and Pierre Gasly took the final point for Alpine. Antonelli made a flying getaway and was 2.3 seconds clear at the end of the opening lap while the Ferrari pair took the fight to slow-starting Verstappen for second place. Leclerc went ahead, before being passed again by the Red Bull, and nearly made contact with Hamilton after the uphill scramble off the grid. The virtual safety car was briefly deployed on lap two to allow marshals to clear debris and Russell was handed a five second penalty for gaining an advantage on Piastri on the opening lap at Turn 13. "I was on the inside, he was overtaking on the outside, that's his risk," said Russell over the radio before the punishment. Haas's Ollie Bearman also collected a 10 second penalty for causing a collision with Gasly and retired at the half-distance.

BRASILIA: Brazil's Supreme Court extended voting in the country's presidential election by two hours on Sunday (Oct 25), leading the electoral authority to pause a vote count that had already started publishing early-stage results. The election pits leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of convicted former President Jair Bolsonaro. Polls were initially set to close at 5pm Brasilia time (4am Monday, Singapore time) and will now close at 7pm after Supreme Justice Cristiano Zanin accepted a request by Lula's campaign to extend voting, pointing to public transportation issues in three cities in the state of Bahia. Zanin's decision landed right around the 5pm cutoff, when the electoral court had already started publishing results that showed Lula leading Bolsonaro with 0.25 per cent of ballot counted. Lula had 57.66 per cent of votes, compared with 42.34 per cent for Bolsonaro, the early count showed.

PAUSE ADDS UNCERTAINTY The pause over the vote count injects uncertainty into a Brazilian electoral process still grappling with the fallout from 2022, when Jair Bolsonaro refused to concede defeat to Lula. His supporters later invaded government buildings in protests against the result, and Bolsonaro received a 27-year prison sentence for plotting a coup. Lula had asked electoral authorities to extend voting in at least nine states after his campaign alleged some officials reduced election day public transportation, impacting voters' ability to get to the polls. Earlier on Sunday, a court in Bahia, a Lula stronghold in the Northeast, ordered the arrest of a top transportation official in the city of Salvador over allegations that he directed a reduction in the city’s bus fleet. Bolsonaro had also asked for voting to be extended in at least three states, citing bad weather.

KYIV: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said US warnings about imminent Russian ballistic missile strikes , critical to Ukraine's air defences, had been fully restored after recent issues. Speaking to Ukraine's TSN television channel, he said SpaceX's Starshield satellite internet had been working at speeds of up to 420kmh since early on Saturday (Oct 24) morning, after it had been throttled earlier in October amid diplomatic pressure on Kyiv from Washington. Zelenskyy said he discussed both issues in a meeting with US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo, casting the changes as results of that meeting. Speaking about the upcoming technical talks between Kyiv, Moscow and Washington in November, Zelenskyy said Ukraine would not discuss limits to its armed forces, or enforced post-war neutrality. Kyiv has long sought entry into the NATO alliance despite the reticence of some members. Zelenskyy also renewed his push for a trilateral US-brokered meeting between him and Vladimir Putin. The Ukrainian leader has long argued Putin is the only person in Russia who can make major decisions to end the war or meaningfully discuss core issues, such as the fate of the nearly 20 per cent of Ukraine that Russia occupies. "The issue of territories is a red line that can be discussed exclusively at the level of leaders," Zelenskyy said.

JERUSALEM: Billionaire American investor Bill Ackman on Sunday (Oct 25) said that Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich should not serve in Israel's next government, saying the two far-right politicians had caused enormous damage to the country's reputation. The public intervention by the prominent hedge fund manager, who is Jewish, comes just two days before Israel's general election, in which polls show a tight race between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition and the opposition. Ackman wrote on X that from the perspective of someone who had an understanding of how Israel was perceived in the United States, "Ben-Gvir and Smotrich have caused Israel enormous reputational damage with their statements and actions." BOTH MINISTERS HAVE FACED SANCTIONS The founder of Pershing Square Capital Management, who praised Netanyahu last week, said a government without the two ministers would send a message that Israel was "turning a new page."

"This will allow Israel to rebuild lost credibility, increase the opportunity for an expansion of the Abraham Accords, and enjoy a better relationship with Democrats and Republicans and Americans at large," he said. The Abraham Accords are the 2020 agreement, mediated by President Donald Trump's first administration, that saw Israel establish relations with the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain. It later reestablished official ties with Morocco. Representatives for Ben-Gvir and Smotrich did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Related:

As ministers in Netanyahu's religious-nationalist coalition, Ben-Gvir and Smotrich have overseen policies widely perceived as discriminatory against Israel's minority Arab population and Palestinians living in the occupied West Bank. Several countries, including Britain, Canada and Australia, have imposed sanctions on the two ministers over accusations that they have incited violence against Palestinians in the West Bank. Ben-Gvir's Jewish Power party is projected to win around 10 parliamentary seats at Tuesday's election, up from 6, while Smotrich's Religious Zionism is projected to win 8, up from 7. Ackman, who was visiting Israel last week, and who along with his wife Neri Oxman owns 5 percent of the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, supported Donald Trump's candidacy for president in 2024. Trump last week publicly endorsed Netanyahu for prime minister. Nimrod Goren, the president of Israeli think tank Mitvim, said Ackman's statement appeared to reflect a desire among Trump's circles for Netanyahu to drop his far-right allies after the vote to form a 'unity government' with opposition parties. However, Gadi Eisenkot, the leading challenger to Netanyahu, and other opposition party leaders have ruled out forming a government with Israel's longest-serving prime minister. Speaking at a Tel Aviv conference on Thursday, Ackman praised Netanyahu, who he said had done a good job in protecting and defending Israel since the Oct 7 2023 Hamas attack. Thousands of Israelis rallied in Tel Aviv on Saturday calling for an independent inquiry into the attack that killed around 1,200 people.

Source: Reuters/fs

MANCHESTER, England, Oct 25 : Manchester United striker Elisabeth Terland scored a late equaliser to knock visitors Manchester City off top spot in the Women's Super League table on Sunday evening as a hotly contested derby finished 1-1 at the Leigh Sports Ground. Reigning champions City dropped points for the first time this season, allowing Chelsea to go top on goal difference after they came back from a goal down to beat Crystal Palace 3-1 earlier in the day.  Chelsea and City both have 19 points, with London City Lionesses third on 16 and Manchester United fourth on 11. Making her 100th WSL appearance, Bunny Shaw gave City the lead in the 66th minute, brushing off the challenge of Dominique Janssen and rattling a shot into the far corner to break the deadlock and silence the home fans, who booed and heckled her throughout.

The game looked to be getting away from United until a well-worked freekick was lofted into the box in the 89th minute, and Norway international Terland was on hand to blast the ball into the net to grab a point for her side. On Merseyside, Liverpool's Jana Fernandez Velasco struck deep into stoppage time to snatch a 2-2 draw at home to London City. Aston Villa raced out to a 3-0 lead over Everton by the 50th minute with Amalie Vangsgaard scoring twice, but the home side scored twice late on to ensure a nervous finish as Villa held on for a 3-2 win. Charlton Athletic's miserable run continued as they slumped to their seventh straight defeat. Substitute Wilma Leidhammar scored the only goal of the game for Birmingham City in the 68th minute to leave Charlton still firmly rooted to the bottom of the table and searching for their first point of the season.

Oct 25 : Pakistan all-rounder Shadab Khan struck an unbeaten 113 and shared a record 89-run last-wicket stand with Haris Rauf as the hosts rallied from 154-9 to secure a one-wicket win over England in Lahore on Sunday and book their place in the tri-series final. Chasing 242 for victory, Pakistan appeared to be heading towards defeat after England's bowlers reduced them to 154-9 in the 34th over. However, Shadab launched a superb counter-attack and, with Rauf making an unbeaten seven off 19 balls, guided the hosts to victory with 17 balls to spare. Their 89-run partnership was the highest for the final wicket in a successful ODI run chase. Earlier, England were bowled out for 241 in 46.4 overs despite Ben Duckett's composed 105. Shaheen Shah Afridi led Pakistan's bowling effort with 4-46 to dismantle England's top order.

The defeat was England's third successive loss in the tri-series after Sri Lanka completed the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history, reaching a target of 430 with one ball to spare. Afridi struck in the opening over to dismiss Tom Banton before removing Joe Root in the third over, while Jordan Cox fell to Haris Rauf as England slumped to 52-4. Ben Duckett and Sam Curran steadied the innings with a fifth-wicket partnership of 93. Curran made 42 before becoming Afridi's third victim. Jamie Overton helped take England past 200, while Gus Atkinson finished unbeaten on 36. Pakistan lost Fakhar Zaman and Babar Azam for 10 apiece before Saad Baig struck a brisk 32 off 22 balls and Salman Ali Agha made 26 to briefly revive the chase. Shadab Khan came to the crease in the 24th over with the hosts struggling at 103-6. Shadab, who struck 13 fours and five sixes, was given out lbw to Atkinson with 21 runs needed, but successfully reviewed the decision after replays showed an inside edge.

Oct 25 : Elon Musk said on Sunday that SpaceX had closed $40 billion in debt financing for graphics processing units, underscoring the soaring cost of building AI computing capacity.  Musk, in a post on X, attributed the successful debt raise to the company's investment-grade status and revenue from its Starlink satellite internet and launch businesses.  It was not immediately clear from Musk’s post what he meant by the deal being “closed” or whether investors had agreed to pricing for the debt. "This is primarily callable debt for GPU purchases that will arrive in Q1 and Q2. Not a major factor this quarter," Musk said in the post.

For the fourth quarter, the company expects $35 billion to $40 billion in capital expenditure, according to Chief Financial Officer Bret Johnsen. Reuters reported earlier this month that SpaceX was in talks with banks and asset managers to raise $40 billion for the purchase of Nvidia artificial intelligence chips. The funding highlights the enormous capital requirement of the AI boom, as technology companies race to secure advanced processors and build out the computing infrastructure needed to support AI development. Musk said debt markets "have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn’t have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers." As a result, he predicted neocloud companies would face significant consolidation and failures, and later said SpaceX won't buy any neoclouds, calling it “pointless.” Unlike larger cloud firms that serve a broad range of industries, neoclouds such as Nebius and CoreWeave mostly focus on tech customers and offer capacity tailored for AI technology. Investors have started betting against US neocloud and data center companies, after fears that their debt-fueled AI buildout was becoming unsustainable sparked a selloff. AI INVESTMENT, CHIP MANUFACTURING SpaceX's revenue climbed 161 per cent from a year ago to $14.58 billion for the three months ended September 30. AI revenue surged by almost 10 times to $7.56 billion, the clearest evidence yet that SpaceX’s heavy investment in AI was paying off. The shift is reshaping a company whose financial engine has long been its Starlink satellite internet services business and whose longer-term ambitions still hinge on getting Starship rockets into regular service.  Terafab, the chip manufacturing joint venture between SpaceX and Tesla in Austin, should produce its first test chip around May or June of next year as it aims to reach volume production by the third quarter of 2028.  Musk told investors in a conference call last week that a merger of his two companies would be "a good idea," citing growing overlap between them. Prior to its blockbuster IPO, SpaceX listed "manufacturing our own GPUs" among the substantial capital expenditures it is undertaking in its S-1 statement, warning prospective investors of its big spending plans to develop AI and other technologies.

Source: Reuters

CARACAS/BARQUISIMETO: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado returned home on Sunday (Oct 25) after nearly a year away, and after several failed attempts to return that strained her ties with US President Donald Trump's administration. "I'm here. With you all," the Nobel Peace Prize- winner wrote on X. LECCE, Italy, Oct 25 : Inter Milan kept pace with Lazio at the top of Serie A after scoring twice in stoppage time to earn a 2–1 home win over Fiorentina on Sunday, while injury-hit Juventus halted their recent slump with a 2–0 victory at Lecce. Fiorentina had looked set to inflict Inter's first league defeat of the season through a second-half goal from Alex Jimenez before Marcus Thuram equalised in stoppage time.  Minutes later, Thuram was brought down in the penalty area by Victor Valdepenas, allowing Piotr Zielinski to convert the resulting spot-kick and seal all three points for the hosts. The late turnaround leaves Inter level on 22 points with Lazio, who won 2–1 at home against Parma on Saturday, while AS Roma are third on 18 points. Fiorentina's third consecutive league defeat means they remain 18th with four points.

LONDON: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he wants a discussion about returning to the European Union's freedom of movement rules for workers, a key issue in the 2016 Brexit referendum which led to Britain leaving the bloc. Building on previous comments about the need to rethink ties with Brussels, Burnham told the Sunday Times that the influx of EU workers into Britain before Brexit had posed very significant challenges. "But, at the same time, it was a type of immigration that perhaps wasn't as difficult (as now)," he said. "Revolving door migration where people would come and then go back is different. The balance of migration has changed, hasn't it, since then? I think we’ve just got to have an honest discussion about those things." Official data has shown long-term net migration in 2025 fell to close to its level before a new post-Brexit immigration system was introduced at the start of 2021.

In September, two months after replacing Keir Starmer as Labour Party leader and prime minister, Burnham said Britain should consider options for its relationship with the EU, including possibly rejoining the bloc one day. He had previously backed the pledges of Starmer's government which included no return to freedom of movement which Brussels sets as a condition for being part of the bloc's single market. In his interview with the Sunday Times, conducted on Oct 19, Burnham said the issue of freedom of movement could be considered as part of a broader reset of Britain's relationship with the EU, including on data sharing and migration.

Related:

Burnham hopes for EU deal next month, stirs Brexit debate

'Welcome back,' says Macron, as UK PM opens door to EU return

"You've got to see it in the round, rather than just looking at freedom of movement on its own," he said. Burnham, who is trying to find ways to speed up Britain's economy, is due to meet top EU officials for a summit on Nov 20. He said he could not imagine recommending that Britain adopt the euro currency or the EU's border-free travel arrangements. A new referendum would be needed to rejoin the EU but not necessarily to join the bloc's single market or a customs union, the Sunday Times quoted Burnham as saying. Former Conservative finance minister Jeremy Hunt, who campaigned to stay in the EU in 2016, said it would be a mistake to reopen one of the fundamental debates of the referendum and he said relaxing immigration rules would hurt people in Britain. "I think it will be a hammer blow to getting people off welfare and into work," Hunt told Sky News.

MANCHESTER, England, Oct 25 : Michael Carrick insisted he was "carrying on as normal" after Manchester United's 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on Sunday, but the manager appeared increasingly vulnerable after a result that left Old Trafford engulfed in anger and resignation. Asked if he expected to still be in charge next week, Carrick offered no guarantees. "Of course, I take responsibility," he said. "Whatever's going to happen, results-wise, whether we win, we lose, draw, whatever happens ... the responsibility is mine." Pressed on whether he expected to be sacked in the coming days, Carrick said: "I totally understand the situation. I'm not expecting anything in particular, to be honest. I'm carrying on as normal, and I love this place.

"I always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club, whatever decision is made on anything really." While Carrick led a resurgent United to third place last season after replacing Ruben Amorim, they have won only twice in 12 matches this campaign across all competitions, and have not won in the top flight since they defeated newly promoted Ipswich Town on August 30. Sunday's defeat left them with seven points from eight league matches, and just a point above the drop zone, their worst return at this stage of a season since 1986-87. Supporters unfurled a giant banner reading "Standards" before halftime featuring club icons Eric Cantona, Roy Keane and Bryan Robson. The fans largely reserved their sympathy for Carrick, singing "It's Carrick you know!" late in the game. But once the 45-year-old tapped a hand to his heart and disappeared down the post-game tunnel, those chants gave way to loud boos directed at the players. The manner of the defeat was almost as damaging as the scoreline. Bournemouth supporters repeatedly taunted Carrick with chants of "You're getting sacked in the morning", while thousands of United fans streamed towards the exits before the final whistle. Former United winger Ashley Young said the performance suggested the squad was no longer responding to its manager. "The fans are behind him and backing him because he's a legend of the football club," Young said on the Sky Sports broadcast. "But the players on the pitch showed nothing. They didn't run, they didn't look like a team together. You could tell today that it was like they'd given up." BRUNO LEFT OUT The pressure on Carrick was intensified by his decision to leave captain Bruno Fernandes on the bench four days after the Portugal midfielder publicly criticised United's tactics following a 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como. Carrick had insisted before kickoff that omitting Fernandes was a "pure football" decision. Television cameras repeatedly caught the midfielder looking dismayed as United lurched towards another defeat. The third goal summed up the chaos. After United lost possession high up the pitch, goalkeeper Senne Lammens raced from his area but completely misjudged a long ball forward, allowing Evanilson to loft the ball into an unguarded net. It was United's afternoon in miniature: disorganised, fragile and punishingly exposed. Harry Maguire, who wore the captain's armband for the day, insisted Carrick had the full support of the dressing room. "We're fully behind Michael (Carrick)," Maguire said. "Coming into the team last season he turned things around and got Champions League football this season. As individuals, we're not playing well enough." Carrick looked close to tears when asked about the supporters' backing after the match. "To be in such a difficult situation and go through a day like we have done and a spell like we have done is certainly difficult to take," he said. "So there's real mixed emotions in there for sure." He rejected suggestions his acknowledgement of supporters after the final whistle had been a farewell. "No, not from me ... just appreciation for the fans and what they've showed me." Former United defender Gary Neville said the crowd's support reflected a belief among fans that Carrick's fate had already been sealed. "The Manchester United fans are singing the Michael Carrick song because I think they know what's going to happen here," Neville said. Even Bournemouth boss Marco Rose expressed sympathy for the beleaguered Manchester manager. "I feel a lot of empathy for my colleagues," he said. "We are just humans, and we try to do our job the best possible way. At the end, it's never easy for us, and I feel with Michael."
